summary: GiftCookie is a specialized kind of Cookie that knows how to wrap itself as a gift. It inherits the flavor and behavior of Cookie, then adds its own small, focused packaging steps that are combined by one public method.

lines.text: The `extends` keyword makes GiftCookie a subclass of Cookie, so every GiftCookie automatically has the fields and methods Cookie already defines.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so GiftCookie needs its own constructor that accepts the flavor a caller wants.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor, letting the parent class initialize the state it owns. It must be the first statement in the constructor.
This is the single public entry point for packaging: callers ask for the whole job in one call instead of remembering three separate steps in the right order.
Calling a method on the same object needs no dot prefix, so the object's own helper is invoked directly here.
Returning a status message lets the calling code report or test the result rather than only watching console output.
Marking the helper `private` hides it from the outside world, so the packaging steps can only be run in the correct order through packageCookie.

lines.code: System.out.println("Packaged " + getFlavor() + " cookie in a box.");
lines.text: getFlavor() is inherited from Cookie, which is why the subclass can read the flavor without declaring that field itself.
Each helper does exactly one thing, which keeps the methods short and easy to name, read, and change later.
The backslash-quote sequence is an escape that puts a literal double quote inside the string, so the note appears in quotation marks.
